title: P7 · Back home
description: Kamal comes home. His GP in Tanavu does not know he was treated in Nalemi. After the story this guide tells.

illustrationStyle.prompt: Warm, flat digital illustration with soft shading and clean outlines, friendly and respectful, in the style of a public-health storybook. Wide banner, aspect ratio 11:4. Bright natural daylight, soft pastel palette with clear colour accents. Faces in gentle three-quarter view with expressive, kind features. Technology shown as simple, oversized icons: a phone with a QR code, a shield with a check mark, a small speech bubble with a symbol. No readable text, no logos, no real brands, no flags with text. All people are fictional.

cast.description: Onesan man, 61, slim, short grey hair, kind face. Batik shirt in Onesa. In Taifafeki, two white pilgrim's garments (unstitched towelling cloth, right shoulder bare when in pilgrim's dress), a small waist pouch and one phone.
His wife, about 58. White modest pilgrimage outfit and white telekung-style hijab in Taifafeki; pastel baju kurung and tudung in Onesa.
Onesan GP, late 30s, tudung, white coat.

notes: Pilgrim's white garments (two white unstitched sheets) is for men only; women wear ordinary modest clothing, usually white, face and hands uncovered.
Keep the shrine and other holy sites far in the background or out of frame.
Keep medical signs text-free so generators don't invent wrong Arabic.

steps.title: Back home
steps.headline: Kamal is home and well, but his GP does not know he was treated in Nalemi.
steps.narrative: Kamal comes home. His GP in Tanavu does not know he was treated in Nalemi. After the story this guide tells.

experiences.doing: Sees Kamal back home, with nothing in her record of his care in Taifafeki.
experiences.feeling: “Treated in Nalemi? Nothing came back to me.”

experiences.doing: Tells her, as best he remembers, what happened.
experiences.feeling: “They gave me a drip… I don't remember what else.”

experiences.doing: Fills in what he does not remember.
experiences.feeling: “Someone should have sent it to her.”

steps.painPoint: The record of care abroad, and who opened his summary, never comes home.
steps.enabler: Nothing yet: the guide does not specify a return path.
steps.policy: Should the host country send a summary of care back to the home country — and with whose consent?
gaps: Nothing returns the record of care in Taifafeki, or a log of who opened his summary, to Onesa.

illustration.alt: Back in Tanavu, Kamal in a white kopiah and Salmah sit with Dr Aisyah, who looks at her computer with a question mark: the record of his care in Taifafeki has not come home.
illustration.prompt: Tanavu: Kamal, healthy, in batik with a white kopiah, sits with Dr Aisyah in her clinic, Salmah beside him. Dr Aisyah looks at her computer with a gentle question-mark bubble: she doesn't know what happened in Taifafeki. To the side, a faint dotted arc from a small Taifafeki building icon toward the clinic fades out halfway with a gap. Warm but slightly unresolved.

record.description: Home again; his GP does not yet know he was treated
